title: Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds
main_claim: Take a klt pair (X,Δ) with rational boundary on a normal, globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold. Then every maximal ordinary negative-ray MMP starting on (X,Δ) terminates. All steps are projective, and the run ends either at a nef adjoint (when K_X+Δ is pseudo-effective, with the usual discrepancy inequalities) or at a projective Mori fibre space with relative Picard rank one.

issues.location: 06-perturbation.tex, Corollary repair:cor:existing and proof of Theorem repair:thm:reduction
issues.description: Termination of the flip tail rests entirely on Theorem 1.1 of the companion paper 'Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (Oct 7). That paper in turn imports this paper's Lemmas 4.1-4.2 and Sections 9-11 (relative steps, gklt threefold termination, special termination, gdlt modification). I checked the internal references and found no cycle: those sections do not cite Section 6, prop:ordinary-step or thm:finite. The only use of prop:ordinary-step there is in Cor 4.x and in Section 12, which the companion does not import. The hypotheses of the companion theorem (projective small diagrams, opposite ample signs, global Weil Q-factorial, M=0) match the ordinary klt flips that occur. Even so, the main theorem holds only if the companion is correct.
issues.evidence: "An infinite run would have an infinite flip tail, contrary to Corollary~\ref{repair:cor:existing}"; companion: "The proof uses the relative constructions and special termination for generalized pairs in \cite{KahlerAuxiliary}"

issues.description: The companion theorem as printed fixes actual canonical divisor representatives. To cover the intrinsic variant of Theorem 1.1 (canonical rational line bundle only), the paper argues that the companion's proof goes through unchanged with local reflexive canonical comparisons. This is only sketched: it says the difficulty, branch argument, Hodge/monodromy steps etc. 'leave that proof unchanged'. It has not been checked against the companion's text in detail. It looks plausible, but it is an unproved adaptation of another paper's proof.
issues.evidence: "Replacing the canonical representatives by these canonical local comparisons therefore leaves that proof unchanged and proves the intrinsic version of Corollary~\ref{repair:cor:existing}."

coverage: I read in full: the introduction and main theorem; Section 3 (integral descent, supports with a Kähler margin, relative positivity, Prop ordinary-step, class transport); Section 4.1 (the cycle-loss lemma via Borel-Moore localization); the start of Section 6, the polarization lemma, the carrier-margin, EMC-transfer, multiplier-ideal-scheme and surface-Mori-base positivity lemmas, Prop negative-part-good-model, the whole restricted induction (C_{d,big}, B_d big and non-big cases, G_d, C_d, order of the induction), Prop supporting-contractions and the final termination theorem; and Section 9 (generalized terminal threefold termination, nef-end comparison, gklt threefold termination). I also mapped every cross-reference in Sections 2, 4 and 8-12 to rule out circular dependence with the Oct-7 companion, and checked that the companion's Theorem 1.1 hypotheses and its citations of this paper (Lemmas 4.1-4.2, Conv. 9.1, Thm 11.3, Prop 11.4) match the numbering here. I did not check in detail: Section 4.2-4.4 (low places, real terminal fourfold termination), Section 8 (relative programs, marked models, extraction), Section 10 (special termination), Sections 11-12, the NQC bound lemmas, or the uniform-index lemmas in Section 9.
sibling_notes: The family 056 board had one entry, for the Sept-24 version of this paper (rank 51, no_gap_found). Its minor note was that projectivity of the flipping contraction in the old Prop 6.4 was not explicitly justified. In this Oct-6 version, Lemma repair:lem:polarization (a global line bundle with α−sD Kähler) addresses that point directly, together with Lemma relative-positivity and Prop supporting-contraction. The companion paper 'Termination of generalized canonical flips' (Oct 6) still cites the Sept-24 version of this paper. The lemmas it uses (2.3 negativity, Section 4.1 cycle counts) keep the same content and numbering here.
